issues.legal_issue: Granting a mining lease transfers a capital asset and may give rise to taxable capital gains.
material_facts: The assessee purchased land and later granted a mining lease permitting a company to extract clay in return for a premium and royalty.
The lease transferred to the lessee a right to exploit the land, a right flowing from the assessee’s ownership of it.
issues.conclusion: The right to exploit the land was a capital asset, and granting the mining lease transferred that asset for consideration, giving rise to capital gains taxable under section 45.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(14), 2(47) and 45 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, property of any kind is a capital asset, and transfer includes the grant of a lease that conveys an interest in land. The Court relied on Traders and Mining Ltd. v. C.I.T. and R.K. Palshikar (HUF) v. Commissioner of Income Tax in treating a lease as a transfer of an asset.

predicates.capital_gains_tax_case: The proceeding concerns whether consideration from transferring an asset is chargeable as capital gains.
predicates.land_owner_grants_mining_lease: The owner of land grants another person a lease to conduct mining on the land.
predicates.lease_conveys_land_exploitation_right: The lease gives the lessee a right to exploit the land by extracting its resources.

issues.definition: When a capital-gains proceeding concerns a landowner who grants a mining lease conveying the right to exploit the land, the grant is treated as a transfer of a capital asset for capital gains.

issues.legal_issue: The cost of acquiring the right to grant a mining lease can be valued and apportioned, allowing capital gains to be computed.
material_facts: The assessee acquired the land for a stated purchase price that included a bundle of rights, including the right to grant a lease.
The right to excavate clay had a monetary value, although valuing it could be difficult.
The cost attributable to the leasehold right could be apportioned on the evidence, using the best valuation possible.
The right to grant the lease was acquired when the assessee acquired the freehold rights.
issues.conclusion: The cost attributable to the leasehold right was capable of determination, so the computation provisions applied and section 45 was attracted. The acquisition date for the right to grant the lease was the date the freehold rights were acquired; C.I.T. v. B.C. Srinivas Shetty was distinguishable because the cost of the right here could be determined.
issues.legal_principle: The cost of an interest transferred by a lease may be apportioned from the acquisition cost of the land because the purchase acquired a bundle of rights that included the right to grant the lease. Apportionment is a question of fact for the tax authority, based on evidence, and the best possible valuation must be made even if it is not mathematically exact; Gold Coast Selection Trust Ltd. v. Inspector of Taxes supports that approach. Because the cost was ascertainable and the right was acquired with the land, the computation provisions and section 45 applied. C.I.T. v. B.C. Srinivas Shetty was distinguished because the asset there had no determinable cost of acquisition.

rule.if: capital_gains_computation_case and land_acquired_with_bundle_of_rights and bundle_includes_right_to_grant_lease and evidence_supports_valuation

predicates.capital_gains_computation_case: The proceeding concerns whether a gain from transferring a lease-related right can be computed for capital gains purposes.
predicates.land_acquired_with_bundle_of_rights: A person acquired land together with the rights attached to ownership of that land.
predicates.bundle_includes_right_to_grant_lease: The ownership rights acquired with the land included the right to grant a lease over it.
predicates.evidence_supports_valuation: Evidence permits a best-possible monetary valuation and apportionment of the cost attributable to the transferred right.

issues.definition: In a proceeding about computing a capital gain from a lease-related right, when land was acquired with the right to grant a lease and the evidence supports valuation, the cost attributable to that right is computable.
